about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Creamy Caesar Dressing
recipes.summary: A thick, garlicky Caesar dressing with anchovy, lemon and parmesan, ready in five minutes.
steps: Mash the anchovies and garlic together into a paste in a bowl.
Whisk in the mayonnaise, lemon juice, mustard and worcestershire sauce until smooth.
Stir in the parmesan, then loosen with the water and season with pepper.
Chill for at least 15 minutes before tossing through cos lettuce.
notes: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.
Also good as a dip for crisp raw vegetables.

recipes.title: Blue Cheese Dip for Wings
recipes.summary: A cool, tangy blue cheese dip to cut through spicy chicken wings and celery sticks.
steps: Mash half the blue cheese with the sour cream and mayonnaise until mostly smooth.
Stir in the buttermilk, lemon juice, garlic and chives.
Fold through the remaining blue cheese so there are chunks, then season with pepper.
Chill for 20 minutes to let the flavours settle.
notes: Thin with a little extra buttermilk for a dressing.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Thousand Island Dressing
recipes.summary: A pink, creamy dressing with pickles and tomato sauce for burgers, slaw and salad.
steps: Combine the mayonnaise and tomato sauce in a bowl until evenly pink.
Stir in the pickles, onion, worcestershire sauce, lemon juice and paprika.
Loosen with the water to a spoonable consistency and chill before serving.
notes: Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.
Spoon over a wedge of iceberg lettuce.

recipes.title: Honey Mustard Dipping Sauce
recipes.summary: Sweet, sharp and four ingredients, a favourite with chicken tenders and sausage rolls.
steps: Whisk the mustard, honey and mayonnaise together until smooth.
Add the lemon juice and salt, then taste and adjust the sweetness.
Serve in a small bowl for dipping.
notes: Keeps for a week in the fridge.
Brush it over chicken thighs in the last 10 minutes of roasting for a sticky glaze.

recipes.title: Chipotle Lime Crema
recipes.summary: Smoky, cooling sour cream sauce for tacos, grilled corn and burrito bowls.

items: 1 chipotle chilli in adobo, finely chopped

steps: Whisk the sour cream and mayonnaise together until smooth.
Stir in the chipotle, adobo sauce, lime juice, garlic and coriander.
Season with salt and chill for 15 minutes before drizzling.
notes: Thin with a splash of water to drizzle from a squeeze bottle.
Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Tartare Sauce
recipes.summary: Classic fish and chip shop sauce with capers, gherkins and fresh parsley.
steps: Mix the mayonnaise with the gherkins, capers, parsley and shallot.
Stir in the lemon juice and pepper, then taste for balance.
Chill for 20 minutes, until the flavours have melded, before serving with crumbed fish.
notes: Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.
Use a little of the gherkin brine for extra tang.

recipes.title: Louisiana Style Remoulade
recipes.summary: A Louisiana style remoulade with mustard, horseradish and paprika for crab cakes and prawns.
steps: Stir the mayonnaise, mustard, horseradish and paprika together in a bowl.
Add the celery, parsley, lemon juice, hot sauce and garlic.
Mix well and chill until cold and the flavours have developed, about 30 minutes.
notes: Serve with crab cakes, boiled prawns or fried green tomatoes.
Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Comeback Sauce
recipes.summary: A Mississippi style dipping sauce, tangy and a little spicy, for chips, burgers and salads.
steps: Whisk the mayonnaise, chilli sauce and ketchup together.
Add the worcestershire sauce, garlic, paprika, hot sauce and lemon juice.
Chill until cold and the garlic has mellowed, about an hour.
notes: Keeps for a week in the fridge.
Excellent on fried chicken sandwiches.

recipes.title: Smoky Barbecue Sauce
recipes.summary: A thick, smoky-sweet sauce simmered from pantry staples for ribs, chicken and burgers.
steps: Combine everything in a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Taste and add a splash of vinegar or a pinch more sugar if needed.
Cool and store in a clean jar.
notes: Keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.
Brush on in the last few minutes of grilling so the sugar doesn't burn.

recipes.title: Smoked Salmon and Dill Brunch Tart
recipes.summary: A crisp pastry case filled with a soft egg custard, smoked salmon and fresh dill.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 23 cm tart tin with the pastry, trimming the edge.
Prick the base, line with baking paper and rice, and bake for 10 minutes. Remove the paper and rice.
Whisk the eggs, cream, milk, dill, spring onions and pepper together.
Scatter the salmon in the case, pour in the custard and bake for 25 minutes until just set with a slight wobble.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
notes: Food safety: bake until the centre is set and reaches 75°C, and keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 2 days.
Serve with a rocket salad.

recipes.title: Baked Eggs in Tomato and Chorizo Pan
recipes.summary: Eggs baked in a spiced tomato and chorizo base, served straight from the pan with bread.
steps: Fry the chorizo in the oil in a large ovenproof pan for 3 minutes until the oil runs red.
Add the onion, garlic and capsicum and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the paprika and tomatoes, then simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the bread.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children, and make sure the chorizo is cooked through to 75°C.
Use a lid or foil if your pan has none.

recipes.title: Ricotta Hotcakes with Berry Compote
recipes.summary: Light, tender hotcakes made with ricotta, served with warm berries and a spoonful of yoghurt.
steps: Simmer the berries and honey in a small saucepan for 5 minutes until syrupy, then keep warm.
Mix the ricotta, egg yolks and milk, then stir in the flour, baking powder and sugar.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks and fold gently into the batter.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan and cook spoonfuls for 2 minutes each side until golden.
Stack the hotcakes, spoon over the berries and add the yoghurt.
notes: Food safety: cook the hotcakes until set through the middle, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Keep cooked hotcakes warm in a low oven.

recipes.title: Lemon Dutch Baby with Fresh Fruit
recipes.summary: A puffed oven pancake with crisp edges and a custardy middle, finished with lemon and berries.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C and place a 25 cm ovenproof frypan inside to heat for 5 minutes.
Blend the eggs, milk, flour, sugar and vanilla until smooth.
Add the butter to the hot pan, swirl to melt, then pour in the batter.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until deeply puffed and golden.
Squeeze over the lemon juice, top with the fruit and dust with icing sugar.
notes: Food safety: bake until the centre is fully set and no longer liquid, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
It sinks as it cools, so serve immediately.

recipes.title: Sheet Pan Breakfast Hash
recipes.summary: Crisp potatoes, capsicum and bacon roasted on one tray with eggs baked in at the end.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C and toss the potatoes, capsicum, onion, bacon, oil, paprika and pepper on a large tray.
Roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until the potatoes are crisp.
Make four hollows, crack an egg into each and bake for 6 to 8 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with chives and serve from the tray.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set and the bacon is cooked through to 75°C.
Use sweet potato for a change.

recipes.title: Brunch Frittata with Zucchini and Feta
recipes.summary: A thick, golden frittata studded with zucchini, fetta and mint, finished under the grill.
steps: Squeeze the grated zucchini in a clean cloth to remove the water.
Cook the onion in the oil in a 24 cm ovenproof frypan for 4 minutes, then add the zucchini and cook 3 minutes more.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mint and pepper, then pour into the pan and scatter the fetta on top.
Cook gently for 6 minutes until the edges set, then grill for 4 minutes until the top is golden and the centre is set.
notes: Food safety: cook the frittata until the centre is fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Delicious cold in a lunchbox.

recipes.title: Egg and Bacon Breakfast Pie
recipes.summary: A classic Aussie bacon and egg pie with a flaky pastry lid, cut into wedges for brunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a 23 cm pie dish with the shortcrust pastry.
Scatter the bacon, cheddar and parsley over the base, then crack the six eggs on top and prick the yolks lightly.
Season with pepper and cover with the puff pastry, sealing the edges.
Brush with the beaten egg and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
notes: Food safety: bake until the eggs are fully set and the bacon is cooked through to 75°C.
Serve with tomato relish.

recipes.title: Avocado and Poached Egg on Seeded Toast
recipes.summary: The cafe favourite at home, with lemony smashed avocado, a soft egg and a sprinkle of seeds.
steps: Toast the sourdough until golden and brush with the olive oil.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice and salt, keeping it chunky.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water for 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Pile the avocado onto the sourdough, then add the eggs, seeds and coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
A splash of white vinegar in the water helps the whites hold together.

recipes.title: Corn Fritter Stack with Bacon and Avocado
recipes.summary: Golden sweetcorn fritters stacked with crisp bacon, avocado and a drizzle of sweet chilli.
steps: Mix the corn, flour, eggs, milk, spring onions and coriander into a thick batter.
Fry the bacon until crisp and set aside.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook spoonfuls of batter for 2 to 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through.
Stack the fritters with bacon and avocado and drizzle with the sweet chilli.
notes: Food safety: cook the fritters until the centres are firm and hot, and the bacon through to 75°C.
Freeze leftover fritters between baking paper.

recipes.title: Big Aussie Brunch Plate
recipes.summary: Eggs, bacon, grilled tomato, mushrooms and avocado on toast, the full weekend plate.
steps: Grill or pan-fry the bacon for 5 minutes until crisp and keep warm.
Fry the tomatoes and mushrooms in the olive oil for 6 to 8 minutes until soft.
Fry the eggs in the butter until the whites are set.
Toast the sourdough until golden and plate everything with the avocado and pepper.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set and the bacon through to 75°C, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Add baked beans if you like.

recipes.title: Chilli and Spring Onion Soft Scramble
recipes.summary: Soft, creamy eggs cooked with fresh chilli and spring onion, piled on buttery toast.
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk and salt together.
Melt half the butter in a non-stick pan and soften the chilli and spring onion for 1 minute.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until just set but still creamy.
Toast the sourdough until golden, butter it, then top with the eggs and coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set and no longer runny, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Leave the chilli seeds out for a milder dish.

recipes.title: Whipped Ricotta Bruschetta
recipes.summary: Grilled sourdough with whipped ricotta, ripe tomatoes, basil and a drizzle of olive oil.
steps: Grill the sourdough until charred at the edges, then rub with the cut garlic.
Mix the tomatoes with half the oil, the vinegar and salt.
Grill until the edges are charred, then spread the ricotta on the toast and spoon over the tomatoes.
Finish with basil and the remaining oil.
notes: Add a poached egg on top for extra protein.
Best made just before eating so the toast stays crisp.

recipes.title: Nostalgic Beef Mince Gravy on Toast
recipes.summary: A retro favourite, tender beef mince in a rich gravy spooned over thick buttered toast.
steps: Brown the mince in the oil in a large pan for 6 minutes, breaking up any lumps.
Add the onion and carrot and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the flour, tomato paste and worcestershire sauce, then pour in the stock.
Simmer for 12 minutes until thick, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Toast the bread until golden, butter it and spoon the mince over.
notes: Food safety: cook the mince until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C throughout.
Leftovers reheat well and freeze for 3 months.

recipes.title: Mushroom and Thyme Brunch Toast
recipes.summary: Garlicky mixed mushrooms with thyme and a swipe of cream cheese on crisp toast.
steps: Heat the butter and oil in a large pan and cook the mushrooms in a single layer over high heat for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Finish with the lemon juice and parsley.
Toast the sourdough until golden, spread with cream cheese and pile on the mushrooms.
notes: Do not crowd the pan, or the mushrooms will steam instead of browning.
Top with a soft egg for a heartier brunch.

recipes.title: Strata with Ham and Cheddar
recipes.summary: A savoury bread and egg bake with ham and cheddar that you can build ahead and bake at brunch.
steps: Grease a 20 x 30 cm baking dish and layer in the bread, ham, cheddar and spring onions.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard and pepper, then pour over the bread and press down.
Stand for 20 minutes so the bread soaks up the custard.
Bake at 180°C for 40 to 45 minutes until puffed, golden and set in the middle.
notes: Food safety: bake until the centre is fully set and reaches 75°C, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Assemble the night before and keep covered in the fridge.

recipes.title: Egg in a Hole Toast
recipes.summary: A fried egg cooked in the middle of a slice of buttered toast, simple and fun for kids.
steps: Cut a round hole from the centre of each slice of bread with a cutter or glass.
Melt the butter in a frypan and toast the bread and the cut-out rounds for 1 minute on one side.
Flip the bread, crack an egg into each hole and season with salt.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are set, then top with chives.
notes: Food safety: cook until the whites are fully set and the yolk thickened, especially for young children, pregnant women and older people.
Dip the toasted rounds in the yolk.
